title: Driver Display Panel and Instruments
summary: Interpret speed, operating state, brake-pressure gauges and warning indications at the driving desk.
objectives: Identify the speedometer and its units
Differentiate brake pipe from brake cylinder labels

sections.heading: Speedometer
sections.body: The speedometer reports train speed, usually in km/h on the configured display. The driver uses it alongside operating restrictions and route instructions. Any permitted-speed display is meaningful only when an appropriate source provides that value.

sections.heading: Brake pressure gauges
sections.body: Where fitted, the brake cylinder gauge and brake pipe gauge report different parts of the braking system. A gauge should be interpreted by its label, units, normal range and the vehicle’s braking arrangement; one gauge cannot substitute for the other.

sections.heading: Operating indications and warning lamps
sections.body: The display can show a selected controller detent, passenger-door status and emergency-brake activity. Warning lamps and messages draw attention to conditions requiring the driver’s awareness, not to software processes.

sections.heading: Cross-checking instruments
sections.body: If power is requested, monitor speed and other relevant indications; if braking is requested, monitor deceleration and the brake response. Do not infer a successful result from the control position alone.

reviewQuestions.question: Which instruments would you compare when practicing a braking request?
reviewQuestions.explanation: Speed change and brake-related indications together help a learner observe the response.

reviewQuestions.question: Do brake pipe and brake cylinder labels mean the same measurement?
choices: No, they refer to different parts of braking systems
reviewQuestions.explanation: Where both are fitted, they are separate measurements and require system-specific interpretation.
